question: What is the average salinity of the Indian ocean?
solution:
The correct answer is ​__**35 **__o/oo.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The common range of ocean salinity ranges between **33-37 grams per liter** **(33 - 37%)**.
 
• In sea water, there are commonly **35 grams of dissolved salts in each liter.**
 
• The salinity in the Indian Ocean is** in the middle of 32 and 37 percent.**
 
• The **highest level of salinity** is in the **Arabian Sea **and along a belt of water situated between** southern Africa and southwestern Australia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The** Atlantic Ocean** has the mo**st excessive salinity of the five oceans**. 
 
• The **slightest saline ocean**, by comparison, is the** Arctic Ocean**, which has a normal** salinity of 28–30 g/kg owing to the low rate of evaporation and meltwater from the ice-caps.**
 
• Ocean salt firstly comes from **rocks on land and openings in the seafloor. **
